question: Can the color content of FLUX.1 [Dev] be isolated as a small, human-interpretable VAE-latent subspace and then used, without model training, both to read emerging color during flow matching and to causally steer an entire image or a selected object toward an arbitrary HSL target?

key_findings.claim: On a deliberately controlled solid-color probe set, FLUX.1's token-averaged VAE latents lie in a three-principal-component geometry that resembles an HSL bicone.
key_findings.evidence: The authors encode N=400 solid-color images sampled uniformly in HSV, average all spatial patches for each image, center the resulting vectors, and report that the first three PCs explain 100% of the measured variance. PC1 orders dark to light, while PC2-PC3 form a hue circle whose radius tracks saturation. This establishes a compact geometry for this probe distribution, but not that every color-dependent degree of freedom in arbitrary textured images is exactly three-dimensional: the inputs themselves vary along only three color coordinates and spatial averaging removes within-image structure.

anchors.section: 3.2 Color Representation in the VAE Space / Figure 2
A Colors in Timestep Experiments

key_findings.claim: The same three-PC, HSL-like organization appears in three additional VAE families, but cross-model evidence is static and preliminary rather than a demonstrated transfer of the observation or intervention algorithm.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix L repeats the solid-color PCA for SD3.5, Qwen-Image, and FLUX.2 and again reports 100% variance in the first three PCs with visually similar organization. No cross-model PRECISE, observation-over-time, intervention, or shared-basis experiment is reported, so the appendix supports recurrence of a low-dimensional probe geometry, not an architecture-independent controller.

key_findings.claim: During FLUX flow matching, average color coordinates follow a strongly time-dependent shift and expansion that the method removes with an empirical axis-wise affine normalization.
key_findings.evidence: For 26 prompts of the form '{color} wall', the token-averaged LCS coordinates remain in similar relative arrangement while moving outward over 50 Euler steps. The method estimates a three-vector shift alpha_t and mean-absolute-deviation scale beta_t from those 26 trajectories, then maps any timestep to the t=50 reference distribution. Appendix G tabulates all 51 shifts and scales; beta at t=0 is only (0.0163, 0.0172, 0.0295), versus (4.9407, 3.8364, 5.2390) at t=50, explaining why early normalization can amplify noise.

key_findings.claim: The advertised LCS-HSL 'bijection' is a closed-form approximation built from eight anchors and geometric assumptions, not an identified global bijection.
key_findings.evidence: Six canonical hue anchors plus encoded black and white define an achromatic axis, hue sectors, and a linearly tapering bicone radius; decoding projects onto this construction and encoding reverses it by spherical interpolation. The construction assumes a circular hue locus and linear maximum attainable distance toward both poles. Moreover, HSL hue is non-identifiable at zero saturation and at black/white, so the mapping cannot be literally one-to-one at those degeneracies; Appendix M is an illustration rather than a proof.

key_findings.claim: LCS projection provides a useful low-cost estimate of emerging average color, sometimes earlier than the final-latent VAE decoder, but it does not reconstruct pixels and retains nonzero error at the terminal step.
key_findings.evidence: On OBJECTS, per-pixel CIEDE2000 error for LCS observation falls from 44 at t=0 to 20 at t=20 and 12 at t=50, versus 26, 15, and 0 for VAE decoding. On WALLS, LCS errors are 45, 11, and 7 versus VAE 33, 19, and 0. For average pixels, LCS is already 13 on OBJECTS and 9 on WALLS at t=10, compared with VAE 13 and 23, respectively. The zero terminal VAE error is definitional because VAE50 is the final image; LCS predicts color only and cannot replace the decoder for content or texture.

key_findings.claim: Successful intervention requires interpolating two individually failing edit geometries in a narrow mid-generation window.
key_findings.evidence: Type I translates all selected LCS patches by the target-minus-current mean; Type II decodes patches to HSL, shifts them there, and re-encodes; Type-star interpolates the two according to the flow scheduler. The qualitative ablation reports that Type I can destroy texture by t=10 and becomes a thin surface recoloring at t=50, Type II has little effect at t=3, early attention masks are unreliable, and late edits retain patch-boundary artifacts. The paper therefore fixes Type-star near steps 8-10 (step 9 for quantitative results), making timing and interpolation essential rather than incidental.

key_findings.claim: On color-category accuracy, LCS control closes most but not all of the gap to explicit color prompting; on continuous color distance it is substantially more precise.
key_findings.evidence: GenEval color accuracy rises from 9% with no color instruction to 68% for local LCS and 72% for global LCS, versus 79% when the target color is written in the prompt. On PRECISE(NATURAL), prompt/local/global CIEDE2000 errors are 23/14/16 and hue errors are 30/14/18 degrees; on PRECISE(PLAIN), prompt/global errors are 20/11 and 24/8 degrees. Thus the mechanism wins on continuous target matching but does not surpass color-explicit prompting on the categorical GenEval measure.

key_findings.claim: Relative to regenerating with a modified prompt, LCS edits better preserve the base image under four grayscale or mask-based structural metrics.
key_findings.evidence: Prompt/local/global LCS obtain IoU 0.60/0.78/0.88, SSIM 0.46/0.59/0.56, LPIPS 0.49/0.35/0.36, and DINOv2 distance 0.36/0.29/0.23. These measurements deliberately ignore color by converting images to grayscale, which is appropriate for structural preservation but cannot detect color-texture artifacts or whether recoloring remains physically plausible.

key_findings.claim: On the reduced 300-image comparison, LCS is markedly better than five control alternatives, but the comparison is neither compute-normalized nor a full-scale, multi-seed benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: For 20 objects, 15 colors, and one seed, local LCS reaches CIEDE2000 10, SSIM 0.62, and LPIPS 0.32. Prompting yields 27/0.48/0.48, best-of-50 yields 19/0.32/0.57, ColorPeel 29/0.22/0.66, ReNO-FLUX 23/0.25/0.61, and IP-Adapter 40/0.29/0.52. The appendix explains that the subset is used because alternatives are expensive, but reports no measured wall time, FLOPs, matched tuning budget, or uncertainty; some methods also solve different conditioning formulations.

key_findings.claim: Subgroup results show that the intervention's strongest advantage is in hue and lightness, while saturation remains difficult at light and dark extremes.
key_findings.evidence: For bright colors, local LCS reduces prompt error from DeltaE 29, hue 28 degrees, saturation 51%, lightness 10% to 11, 8 degrees, 28%, and 7%. For muted colors it reaches 14, 16 degrees, 19%, and 6% versus prompt 21, 28 degrees, 21%, and 10%. But for light colors local LCS saturation error is 53% versus prompt 54%, and for dark colors it is 55% versus prompt 53%, despite improvements in DeltaE, hue, and lightness. The HCL/CIELAB appendix likewise supports broad color improvement without eliminating this specific weakness.

key_findings.claim: Localized and repeated control is possible in the shown examples, but it depends on a separate spatial-selection mechanism and has only qualitative multi-object evidence.
key_findings.evidence: The local method obtains masks from Seg4Diff cross-attention at transformer layer 18 (or from GenEval's detector in PRECISE), then edits only the corresponding latent patches. Appendix C shows two simultaneous object-specific interventions, including touching or overlapping objects, but supplies no multi-edit accuracy, leakage, or identity-preservation metric. Consequently the local pipeline is training-free with respect to color parameters, yet not localization-free or solely an LCS computation.

key_findings.claim: Fine-detail preservation and color integration impose an explicit timing-versus-mask-quality tradeoff that the main aggregate scores do not resolve.
key_findings.evidence: The main method intervenes at t=9 so the remaining trajectory can integrate color, but Appendix H acknowledges that early modification can change fine semantics, such as making a red steak appear raw or a green stump mossy. Moving the edit to t=20-25 preserves more details only when cleaner bounding boxes are available. This is a useful negative result: a single default timestep cannot simultaneously maximize integration, localization robustness, and exact source-image preservation.

method.core_idea: Calibrate a three-dimensional PCA basis for solid-color FLUX VAE latents, interpret its geometry as approximate HSL coordinates, normalize its distribution across flow-matching timesteps, and manipulate selected patch coordinates in that basis before projecting them back into the original latent trajectory.
method.mechanism: Four hundred spatially uniform HSV samples define the PCA basis and mean. Six hue images plus black and white define a closed-form bicone map between LCS and HSL. Twenty-six generated wall-color trajectories define per-timestep shift alpha_t and axis-wise scale beta_t relative to t=50. To observe color, each latent patch is projected, time-normalized, and decoded to HSL. To intervene, the selected patch cloud is shifted either directly in LCS (Type I) or after HSL decoding and re-encoding (Type II); a scheduler-weighted Type-star blend is denormalized to the current timestep and replaces only the three LCS components. Global edits select every patch; local edits select patches using a segmentation or detector mask.
assumptions: Spatially averaged solid-color encodings expose the same color geometry used for textured, shaded, and multi-object images.
Three PCA components contain the causally relevant color signal rather than merely explaining the variance of an intrinsically three-parameter calibration set.
The three-PC locus is well approximated by an HSL bicone whose hue sectors can be fixed by six anchors and whose radius decays linearly toward black and white.
Calling the mapping a bijection is operational shorthand despite HSL's undefined hue at zero saturation and at the lightness poles.
Across prompts and images, timestep drift is adequately removed by one global three-vector shift and independent per-axis mean-absolute-deviation scale estimated from 26 colored walls.
The t=50 calibration and the 50-step Euler schedule match the inference schedule on which the method is deployed.
Uniformly shifting all selected patches preserves their non-color semantics and leaves discarded latent dimensions sufficient for texture and shape.
The target object mask is accurate in latent-patch coordinates; segmentation leakage is not part of the color mechanism but directly affects local outcomes.
Average masked image color is an adequate target for objects with shading, reflections, transparency, or multiple materials.
Grayscale SSIM, LPIPS, DINOv2 distance, and detector-mask IoU adequately represent non-color preservation.
The small, one-seed competitor subset is representative despite different backbones, conditioning interfaces, and computational budgets.

techniques.role: Identifies a three-coordinate VAE subspace from token-averaged encodings of controlled colors.
Uses six hue anchors and black/white poles to construct closed-form approximate LCS-to-HSL encoding and decoding.
Maps intermediate LCS distributions to the terminal reference with per-step shifts and axis-wise scales.
Predicts patch and average color from three latent coordinates without running the 50-million-parameter VAE decoder.
Type I preserves patch offsets while translating the selected cloud mean to the target LCS coordinate.
Type II alters hue, saturation, and lightness after decoding individual patches and then re-encodes them.
Type-star blends Type I and Type II so early edits influence the trajectory without the texture loss of direct late translation.
Restricts intervention to object patches using Seg4Diff layer-18 attention or detector masks.
Evaluates 51 HSL targets with perceptual, hue, saturation, lightness, and structural metrics beyond color-name accuracy.

evaluations.setting: FLUX.1 VAE, 400 spatially uniform colors sampled in HSV and averaged over latent patches; appendix replication on SD3.5, Qwen-Image, and FLUX.2.
evaluations.metric: PCA explained variance and qualitative alignment of PC geometry with hue, saturation, and lightness.
evaluations.result: The first three PCs explain 100% of measured variance for all four tested VAEs; FLUX PC1 tracks lightness and PC2-PC3 trace a saturation-scaled hue circle.
evaluations.baseline: The remaining VAE latent dimensions and the hypothesis that color is distributed without a compact geometric organization.

evaluations.setting: Twenty-six single-color wall prompts over the complete 51-step FLUX trajectory.
evaluations.metric: Token-averaged LCS position, per-timestep shift alpha_t, and centered mean-magnitude scale beta_t.
evaluations.result: Relative color arrangement remains visually consistent while expanding; beta grows from (0.0163, 0.0172, 0.0295) at t=0 to (4.9407, 3.8364, 5.2390) at t=50.
evaluations.baseline: Using terminal LCS-HSL coordinates at every timestep without temporal normalization.

evaluations.setting: GenEval single-object images (OBJECTS) and 26 single-color walls (WALLS), compared at t in {0,10,20,30,40,50}.
evaluations.metric: Per-pixel and average-pixel CIEDE2000 distance to the final image.
evaluations.result: Per-pixel LCS errors are OBJECTS 44/31/20/14/12/12 and WALLS 45/23/11/8/7/7; VAE-decoded errors are 26/21/15/9/4/0 and 33/25/19/12/5/0. Average-pixel LCS errors are 37/13/11/11/10/10 and 40/9/7/7/7/7, versus VAE 16/13/9/6/2/0 and 31/23/18/11/5/0.
evaluations.baseline: Directly decoding each intermediate latent with FLUX's 50-million-parameter VAE decoder.

evaluations.setting: GenEval color task with unchanged object-only prompts; global and Seg4Diff-local Type-star intervention at timestep 9.
evaluations.result: No color instruction scores 9%; local LCS scores 68%; global LCS scores 72%; explicit color prompting scores 79%.
evaluations.baseline: The same generation without any color input and a prompt that names the color.

evaluations.setting: PRECISE(NATURAL): 20 GenEval objects x 51 HSL colors x 4 seeds = 4,080 images; PRECISE(PLAIN): ten prompt-seed pairs selected for spatially uniform outputs across the same colors.
evaluations.metric: CIEDE2000, absolute hue degrees, saturation percentage, and lightness percentage relative to target.
evaluations.result: On NATURAL, prompt/local/global obtain DeltaE 23/14/16, hue 30/14/18 degrees, saturation 43/37/33%, and lightness 14/6/9%. On PLAIN, prompt/global obtain 20/11, 24/8 degrees, 36/22%, and 13/8%.
evaluations.baseline: Color-explicit prompting and object-only prompting without color.

evaluations.setting: GenEval base generations compared with prompt-regenerated and LCS-recolored counterparts after grayscale conversion.
evaluations.metric: Detector-mask IoU and grayscale SSIM, LPIPS, and DINOv2 distance.
evaluations.result: Prompt/local/global score IoU 0.60/0.78/0.88, SSIM 0.46/0.59/0.56, LPIPS 0.49/0.35/0.36, and DINOv2 distance 0.36/0.29/0.23.
evaluations.baseline: Adding the target color to the prompt and regenerating with the same base model.

evaluations.setting: PRECISE(NATURAL,SMALL): 20 objects x 15 colors x one seed = 300 images, used because several alternatives require per-color training or per-image optimization.
evaluations.metric: CIEDE2000, SSIM, and LPIPS; appendix also reports hue, saturation, and lightness errors.
evaluations.result: Local LCS achieves DeltaE 10, SSIM 0.62, LPIPS 0.32; prompt is 27/0.48/0.48, BoN-50 with a color prompt 19/0.32/0.57, ColorPeel 29/0.22/0.66, ReNO-FLUX 23/0.25/0.61, and IP-Adapter 40/0.29/0.52. Appendix hue/saturation/lightness for local LCS are 12 degrees/25%/7%.
evaluations.baseline: Prompting, best-of-N for N in {10,20,50}, ColorPeel, ReNO on SDXL and FLUX, and IP-Adapter.

evaluations.setting: PRECISE(NATURAL) split into bright, muted, light, and dark HSL targets.
evaluations.metric: CIEDE2000 and hue, saturation, and lightness component errors.
evaluations.result: Local LCS bright/muted/light/dark DeltaE is 11/14/17/16 and hue error is 8/16/16/16 degrees. Saturation error is 28/19/53/55%, showing little or no advantage over prompting on light (54%) and dark (53%) targets.
evaluations.baseline: No-color and explicit-color prompts, plus global LCS intervention.

evaluations.setting: Qualitative continuous hue, saturation, and lightness sweeps; two simultaneous object edits; later-timestep detail-preservation examples.
evaluations.metric: Visual continuity, edit locality, color diversity, and preservation of fine details.
evaluations.result: Figures show six-step red-to-magenta, blue-to-grey, and white-through-red-to-black sweeps, two different recolorings in one image, and improved detail when moving edits to t=20-25 with cleaner boxes; no quantitative leakage or multi-edit success rate is supplied.
evaluations.baseline: The t=9 default, a single intervention, and color changes made through prompt, BoN, ColorPeel, ReNO, or IP-Adapter.

limitations: Author-demonstrated: Type I, Type II, early, and late interventions each fail differently; the selected Type-star/t=9 setting is a qualitative compromise rather than a universally optimal rule.
Author-demonstrated: early edits can alter fine semantics, while later t=20-25 edits require cleaner boxes and may integrate color less naturally.
Author-stated: the SD3.5, Qwen-Image, and FLUX.2 results are preliminary evidence of generality; full observation and intervention evaluations remain FLUX.1-only.
Reviewer-identified: 100% explained variance on solid-color inputs does not prove that all color in arbitrary imagery is confined to exactly three VAE dimensions.
Reviewer-identified: the LCS-HSL mapping is not literally bijective at achromatic colors or lightness poles and is calibrated from only eight canonical anchors.

Reviewer-identified: the method is training-free but not calibration-free; it needs 400 encoded colors, anchor encodings, 26 full trajectories, a fixed sampler schedule, and stored per-timestep statistics.
Reviewer-identified: local intervention depends on Seg4Diff or detector masks, so localization quality and leakage are external bottlenecks that the color-subspace analysis does not solve.
Reviewer-identified: the 4,080-image main benchmark measures average masked color and can underrepresent gradients, material-specific reflectance, transparency, and multicolor preservation.
Reviewer-identified: structural metrics are grayscale and therefore do not penalize implausible chromatic texture or color-dependent semantic changes.
Reviewer-identified: the five-method comparison has only 300 images and one seed, lacks uncertainty and measured compute, and compares methods with different backbones or conditioning goals.
Reviewer-identified: saturation errors remain around 52-55% for light and dark targets, so the HSL interpretation does not yield equally precise control along all three claimed axes.
failure_modes: At t near zero, tiny beta_t values amplify noise and attention masks have not stabilized, so edits can alter global semantics or the wrong patches.
Direct LCS translation at later timesteps collapses or distorts patch variation, losing texture or producing a superficial painted layer.
HSL-domain edits too early can have negligible final influence because per-patch color has not yet emerged.
Very late edits leave sharp patch boundaries because too few flow steps remain to clean artifacts.
Incorrect, coarse, or overlapping object masks recolor background or neighboring objects; the intervention itself has no mechanism for correcting mask leakage.
The six-anchor circular interpolation can mis-estimate colors whose VAE locus departs from the assumed bicone, especially near achromatic and lightness-pole degeneracies.
Changing the sampler, number of Euler steps, VAE, checkpoint, or latent scaling invalidates alpha_t, beta_t, PCA basis, and anchor coordinates unless they are recalibrated.
Objects whose perceived color is spatially multimodal, reflective, transparent, or illumination-dependent can be poorly represented by a single selected-cloud mean.
Large saturation edits near light or dark poles are ill-conditioned because the assumed attainable chroma radius approaches zero.
Optimizing average target color can flatten realistic shading even when grayscale similarity remains high.
reusable_insights: Probe perceptual attributes with controlled stimuli, but separately test whether a low-dimensional probe manifold captures within-image, textured, and causal variation.
Treat temporal generative trajectories as moving coordinate distributions; an interpretable terminal basis may need explicit step-wise calibration before it is meaningful mid-generation.
When two edit parameterizations fail at opposite ends of a trajectory, a scheduler-aware interpolation can be more stable than choosing either one globally.
Preserve all latent components orthogonal to a causal attribute subspace and intervene only on selected patch coordinates to reduce collateral changes.
Report categorical adherence, continuous perceptual distance, component-wise color errors, structure preservation, and locality because each exposes different failures.
Audit achromatic and boundary cases whenever cylindrical or polar perceptual coordinates are described as bijective.
Separate 'no learned parameters' from 'no calibration data': closed-form controllers can still be checkpoint- and schedule-specific.
Evaluate control methods on matched compute and conditioning interfaces; qualitative claims of low cost are not substitutes for timings or FLOPs.
Expose timing-versus-localization tradeoffs rather than presenting one intervention step as universally optimal.
open_questions: Does the same three-dimensional basis causally control SD3.5, Qwen-Image, and FLUX.2, or do only their solid-color probe manifolds look similar?
How much color information about textures and spatial gradients remains outside the first three PCs when patches are not averaged?
Can the time normalization be predicted analytically from the flow schedule or estimated online, avoiding 26 calibration trajectories and sampler lock-in?
Would a nonlinear, uncertainty-aware manifold map outperform the eight-anchor bicone specifically for low-saturation, light, and dark colors?
How robust are PRECISE results across random calibration colors, PCA seeds, prompt sets, samplers, guidance scales, step counts, and FLUX checkpoint revisions?
Can object localization and color intervention be coupled so that the method measures and corrects leakage rather than assuming a mask?
How should multicolor objects, transparency, specular reflections, and illumination gradients be represented without collapsing them to an average HSL target?
Do direct interventions in LCS change only color under causal feature tests, or do they also alter material, temperature, mood, and object identity in ways grayscale metrics miss?
Can one derive an invertible perceptual coordinate chart that handles HSL pole degeneracies without calling a many-to-one representation a bijection?
How does LCS compare with ColorWave and Color Alignment under identical backbone, target set, runtime, memory, and localization masks?

competitive_landscape.title: Color encoding in Latent Space of Stable Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest direct predecessor on mechanistic color geometry in diffusion VAE latents.
competitive_landscape.difference: Arias et al. use controlled synthetic data, PCA, and similarity analysis to identify circular opponent-color structure mainly in Stable Diffusion latent channels c3-c4 and intensity/shape in c1-c2. LCS studies a learned three-PC FLUX VAE basis, adds time-dependent flow calibration, decoder-free observation, and causal intervention; therefore the static low-dimensional color-encoding claim overlaps, while prediction and control are the narrower added combination.

competitive_landscape.title: ColorPeel: Color Prompt Learning with Diffusion Models via Color and Shape Disentanglement
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct precise-color generation baseline and explicit competitor in the paper's reduced benchmark.
competitive_landscape.difference: ColorPeel learns color tokens from colored 2D/3D shapes and uses a cross-attention alignment loss to separate color from shape; its per-color optimization is training-based. LCS instead recalibrates a fixed FLUX VAE coordinate system once and applies arbitrary HSL targets in closed form, but is checkpoint/schedule-specific and needs external masks for local edits.

competitive_landscape.title: Color Alignment in Diffusion
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct diffusion color-control method that constrains generation through a color-space projection.
competitive_landscape.difference: Shum et al. align image samples or latent diffusion terms to an input color pattern/distribution, targeting coverage, proportion, and disentanglement of multiple prescribed colors. LCS instead discovers an HSL-like FLUX VAE subspace and shifts a whole image or masked object's mean toward one target while also exposing mid-generation color; it does not directly enforce a spatial palette pattern.

competitive_landscape.title: Leveraging Semantic Attribute Binding for Free-Lunch Color Control in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest training-free competitor for exact arbitrary-color control.
competitive_landscape.difference: ColorWave obtains RGB-level control by analyzing and rewiring color-text/reference-feature binding inside IP-Adapter cross-attention. LCS uses no adapter binding: it interprets and edits a calibrated three-dimensional FLUX VAE basis and additionally reads color over flow time, but its local version depends on segmentation and its calibration does not transfer unchanged across models or samplers.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first demonstration that FLUX color lives in a three-dimensional HSL-like VAE subspace, the first full-HSL functional interpretation that predicts color throughout flow matching, and a novel entirely training-free, localized intervention based solely on mechanistic latent manipulation.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The 400-color PCA, 26-trajectory temporal calibration, closed-form eight-anchor mapping, decoder-free observation, Type-star ablation, PRECISE evaluation, and structural-preservation comparison jointly show a working FLUX-specific interpret-and-control pipeline. The appendix reproduces only the static geometry on three other VAEs. The paper itself acknowledges concurrent color-encoding analysis by Arias et al.; current primary records also include ColorWave's training-free exact-color control and Color Alignment's color-space projection.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the specific combination of an empirically discovered FLUX VAE color basis, explicit flow-time normalization, decoder-free observation, and scheduler-interpolated causal editing. A broad claim that color is first shown to have low-dimensional circular latent structure is weakened by the concurrent Stable Diffusion analysis, and 'solely' mechanistic/localized control should be narrowed because the pipeline uses calibration datasets and external segmentation. The cross-model appendix supports a promising recurring geometry, not yet a universal controller.

reviewer_notes: Read the extracted 26-page text end to end, including all references and Appendices A-M. Formula extraction on pages 3-6 is visually compressed but preserves the definitions needed for the audit; all quantitative values were cross-checked against Tables 1-8 and appendix settings. The PDF extraction index reports usable text on all 26 pages, so no anchor targets a missing page. Competitor identities, exact titles, and latest source revisions were checked on direct arXiv records on 2026-08-23: 2512.09477 v1, 2407.07197 v1, 2503.06746 v1, and 2503.09864 v2; official CVPR 2025 and WACV 2026 proceedings records were also consulted to confirm the latter two venue identities. Confidence is high for the reported FLUX experiments and formulas, and lower for the paper's universal-subspace and literal-bijection language because the probes, cross-model evidence, and achromatic boundary cases do not establish those stronger claims.
